rendered: In the BatPaC scenario for the projected EV fleet, the document says that with NMC 111[1] as the cathode of choice, the total cobalt required would be ≈2500 tons[2] of cobalt. For the next-generation NMC 811[3] and NCA cathodes, the document says they would still require ≈700 tons of cobalt[4] to realize the same scenario. By contrast, for NFA the document states that if NFA cathodes were deployed for the same number of EVs, range and pack energy, no cobalt would be required[5]. The text gives these totals; the per-class cobalt bars are shown in the Figure panel of the BatPaC results.
